answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable deposit before it can submit a market order; the protocol releases the deposit only after a randomly selected challenge is answered and the order settles without a proven duplicate identity. This does not prove a personhood, but it makes Sybils costly: an attacker multiplying identities must immobilize capital for every one and risks forfeiting deposits on failed challenges. Copper, cedar, and gale can name challenge rounds without changing the rule.
